critical_obligations.physical_sufficiency: For fixed Schmidt witness W, arbitrary global-unitary trace equals sum(lambda_i*w_j*|U_ji|^2). The squared-modulus matrix is doubly stochastic, so spectral rearrangement bounds it below by an adverse permutation. Such a permutation assigns top R to negative slots and bottom K to positive slots, hence is included among the pattern matrices. This also covers Schmidt vectors with zero coordinates.
critical_obligations.precompactness_coercivity: Clipping residual is controlled by actual l2 bound independently of c. Interval deficit gap D[B(t)-B(kappa)] is at least a positive multiple of c_m. Therefore bounded-below correction forces bounded c_m before prefix compactness or singular derivatives are invoked.
critical_obligations.small_order_non_circularity: For bounded c, (19) applied to a pattern containing beta1 on a diagonal forces its Perron root uniformly below two; beta1 therefore stays uniformly below one. This uses the physical rank-one inequality, not the asymptotic entropy identity (17).
critical_obligations.no_escaped_mass: First walk term for every omitted slot contributes exactly 2T_tail/a^2, without requiring disjoint remaining physical slots. It yields c>=C(prefix)+2 liminf T_tail. Tail gain is O(1/L), so optimality forces uniformly vanishing l1 tail mass.
critical_obligations.infinite_profile_equality: All star and strict-interaction arguments are first valid on finite prefixes. At bounded cost their resolvent gaps are uniform, and summability lets U,S and gains pass to the limit; finite-prefix cost supremum defines the infinite cost. Critical multi-anomaly profiles retain a strict positive interaction from two fixed nonzero entries.
critical_obligations.all_near_maximizers: Loss estimates imply both J_m->0 and uniform l1 tail control. Any subsequence has an l1/c convergent subsubsequence satisfying C<=c and (27). Equality forces c=C. Compactness gives the distance criterion for the entire sequence; converse follows by gain/penalty continuity and (17).
